title: Quick Tip: Power BI Sharing Options Explained — What to Use, When, and Why
summary: Power BI offers six distinct sharing methods for reports, each with different security levels and licensing requirements. This post explains when to use Publish to Web for public data, Secure Embed for internal authenticated users, Power BI Embedded for external customers, URL Filters for prefiltering, Power BI Apps for curated collections, and Template Apps for partner distribution.
key_points: Publish to Web requires no authentication but offers no security and is suitable only for public non-sensitive data
Secure Embed enforces organizational authentication and permissions, best for internal portals and authenticated users
Power BI Embedded uses an app-owns-data model for external customers who lack Power BI accounts, requiring capacity-based licensing
URL Filters enhance user experience through query parameters but are not a security mechanism
Power BI Apps bundle multiple reports for centralized distribution to internal and guest users with flexible licensing
